By this award, I shall decide a claim petition under section 166/140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
filed by the petitioners - Pramila Rani Goyal (wife of the deceased), Sushil Kumar Goyal & Gourav Goyal (sons of the deceased), Manisha Aggarwal & Pushpa Rani (daughters of the deceased) with respect to the death of Satish Chand Goyal in a motor vehicle accident.
2. It is the case of the petitioners that the accident in the present case took place on 20.06.2016 at around 06:15 in the morning.

Satish Chand Goyal was going on his scooter registration No.
DL-5S-AS- 0583 to park for morning walk.

When he reached on the road in front of Sector 15-A Noida, Abhitab Park, G.B. Nagar, he was hit by a speeding car registration No. UP-14BR-5480 driven by its driver respondent no. 1 Phooleshwar from behind.
Due to this accident, Satish Chand Goyal suffered grievous injuries.
He was taken to Kailash Hospital where he passed away on 25.06.2016.
For this accident, FIR No.905/2016 was registered in Police Station Sector-20 Gautam Budh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh under section 279/338 of the Indian Penal Code on 20.06.2016.

entities.text: Police Station Sector-20 Gautam Budh Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: According to the claim petition, Satish Chand Goyal was a self employed person.
He was running a shop of general merchant at Delhi and was earning about Rs.2,74,215/- per annum.
The petitioners have claimed Rs.One Crore as compensation for the death of Satish Chand Goyal in that motor vehicle accident.
3. The respondent no. 1 Phooleshwar and respondent no.2 Manish Kumar, who are the driver and owner of the offending vehicle have taken the defence that they have been falsely implicated in this case.

The number of the vehicle given in the FIR which was registered promptly on the same, was UP 14BR 5400 and it was stated to be a cab, wheres as the number of the offending vehicle implicated in the present case is different.
It is not clear on what basis the vehicle of these respondents have been implicated in this case.
It is also alleged that the alleged eye witness Yusuf is a planted witness and his conduct shows that he was not even present on the spot at the time of accident.
It is further alleged that none of the petitioners were dependent on the deceased.
The vehicle was not in use and that is why it was not insured.
4. Since the vehicle was not insured, there is no insurance company as respondent.

sentences.text: On the basis of the pleadings of the parties following issues were framed on 01.11.2017 - (i) Whether Mr. Satish Chand Goyal died in a motor vehicular accident on 20.06.2016 at about 6.15 a.m. in front of Sector 15A, Noida, Abhitab Park, Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P. within jurisdiction of PS Sector20, Noida due to rash and negligent driving of motor vehicle bearing registration No. UP 14 BR 5480 by the respondent No. 1?(OPP)
(ii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

(OPP)
(iii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate of interest and for which period?(OPP)
(iv) Relief?
6.
In order to establish their claim, petitioners examined Sh. Sushil Kumar Goyal as PW-1 and PW-2 Yusuf as an eye witness.
7. In their defence, both the respondents examined themselves.
8. I have heard Mr. Pratap Singh, counsel for petitioners and Mr. Rajiv R Raj, counsel for no. 1 & 2 and perused the records.

9. The issues are decided as follows- ISSUE No.1: Whether Mr. Satish Chand Goyal died in a motor vehicular accident on 20.06.2016 at about 6.15 a.m. in front of Sector 15A, Noida, Abhitab Park, Gautam Budh Nagar, U.P. within jurisdiction of PS Sector20, Noida due to rash and negligent driving of motor vehicle bearing registration No. UP 14 BR 5480 by the respondent No. 1? (OPP)
10.
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the preponderance of probabilities which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further in holding any inquiry under section 168, the Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
11. Now in this case, the petitioners examined Sushil Kumar Goyal as PW-1.
He is the son of the deceased Satish Chand Goyal.

In order to establish the claim of petitioners, he has proved the documents like the copies of aadhaar cards of the petitioners income tax returns of his father,
documents of offending vehicle, medical treatment records and bills etc.
He has deposed that deceased Satish Chand Goyal was his father, who was aged about 57 years at the time of accident and that his father died on 25.06.2016 in the Kailash Hospital.

He has also deposed about the manner of accident but since he is not an eye- witness of the accident, his testimony regarding that Pramila Rani & Others vs Phooleshwar & Another on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65240140/
3 aspect is of no relevance.

sentences.text: 12. Regarding negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle in this accident, the only evidence is of the eye witness PW-2 Yusuf.

He deposed that on one day in 2016 at about 06:00 a.m. to 06:30 a.m., he was going to Amitab Park from his house and when he reached in front of gate no. 1 of Sector-15A, Noida, he heard some noise from other side of the road.
Then, he crossed the road and went toward the accident site and saw that a car make Indica, colour-white, registration number UP-14-5480 was going away from the place of accident.
There a scooty, whose number he does not remember, and the injured were lying on the ground.
Public persons also gathered there.
He left for his house.

After about 5-6 days of accident, when he was going to his construction site at New Ashok Nagar, he found that several people had gathered in a nearby house and on inquiry, he came to know that resident of that house had passed away.
On making further inquiry, he came to know that the deceased was the same person who was injured in the aforesaid accident.
Then he informed one of the family members namely Mani (PW-1 Sushil Kumar Goyal) and few other persons present there that he had seen the accident and the offending vehicle.
13. Now, the testimony of this witness shows that probably he had not seen the accident.
In examination in chief he states that after hearing some noise, he went to the other side of the road and saw a speeding car.
He saw the scooty and the injured lying on the road and then went away to his home.
In his cross examination, he admitted he know the deceased who had a grocery shop at around one kilometer from his house.

I do not understand what kind of human being this witness is,
who has seen that his acquaintance was injured in the accident and lying on the road and without helping him in any manner whatsoever he left his home.
He has seen the offending vehicle according to his evidence despite that did not wait and gave its number to the police.
He did not took any pains to help the injured.
He admitted that after the accident he did not inform the family members of victim despite knowing about the shop of the deceased in the vicinity of his house.
He did not went to the police station to lodge a complaint.
This is not a natural conduct of a person.
It shows that he was not present there and did not see the accident.
His evidence at most suggest that he only saw the speeding vehicle and not the accident.
14. The manner in which this witness has came in picture is also doubtful.
It is an admitted fact that he lives in the same locality of the deceased and also know the deceased.
On the date of death of the deceased, he informed the family members that he had seen the accident.

It was probably after 7-8 days when the number of the offending vehicle might have come in picture after which on 09.07.2016 the son of the deceased wrote a letter to the police to change the number of the offending vehicle in the accident.
The son of the deceased has admitted that on the instance of Mohd Yusuf, he subsequently wrote a letter to the police to change the vehicle number.
Mohd Yusuf told about the correct registration number of the offending vehicle after about 10 days of the accident.
The son of the deceased Sushil Kumar Goyal PW-1 told this witness that the details of the vehicle seized by the police was not matching with the vehicle mentioned in the FIR.
From the record, it prima facie appears that this sole eye-witness was known to the family of the deceased and therefore his being an interested witness cannot be ruled out.

From his examination-in-chief and his conduct subsequent to the accident, he cannot be considered as a reliable witness to come to a conclusion that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the respondent no.1.

sentences.text: In the FIR, a different vehicle number was mentioned.
It is not clear how then the offending vehicle of the present case was got identified as being involved in the accident.
Both the respondents have entered the witness box and deposed that they have been falsely implicated in this case.
The person who made call to the police after the accident has not been cited as a witness either in the chargesheet or in these proceedings.
There is nothing much in their cross examination to impeach their credit.

16. The overall evidence in this case shows that the eye-witness, has not been able to prove even by preponderance of probabilities that he was present at the place of accident or that he saw the accident and therefore cannot be termed as the eye-witness.
Therefore, it cannot be said on the basis of his testimony that the accident happened due to the fault or negligence of respondent no. 1.
He is the acquaintance of the deceased and therefore no doubt would have been interested in a favourable outcome of this case.

17. In the case of Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors., 2009 ACJ 1725, though it was observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that strict proof of accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants but, it was clearly mentioned that the core question before the Tribunal should be whether the vehicle in question was involved in the accident or not.

entities.text: Bimla Devi & Ors. Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors., 2009 ACJ 1725
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: One of the argument of petitioners is that the chargesheet has been filed in this case against respondent No.1 which shows that his vehicle was involved and the vehicle was driven negligently.
But it cannot be lost sight of the fact the witnesses on the basis of which the investigation officer filed the chargesheet had flunked before this Tribunal and not found reliable.
Therefore, merely filing of chargesheet has no benefit to the claimants.

18. Therefore, on the basis of preponderance of probabilities, though it has been proved that the deceased Satish Chand Goyal died due to a road accident but petitioners failed to prove that the accident in which he was injured and consequently died was caused due to the negligence of respondent no. 1, the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, this issue no.1 is decided in favour of the respondents and against the petitioners.
Issue No. 2, 3 & 4 : (ii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?
(OPP), (iii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to interest on the award amount, if so, at what rate of interest and for which period?(OPP) and (iv) Relief?
19. These issues are decided simultaneously.
Section 166 MV Act is based on the principle of fault liability.
To seek compensation under this section the claimant has to prove that the cause of the accident was the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In the case of New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Devki & others- Neutral Citation No. 2016:DHC:1735 dated 29.02.2016 of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, it was held that it is well settled that in proceeding arising out of a claim petition under Section 166 of MV Act based on fault liability principle, a person cannot be held liable unless he contravenes any of the duties imposed on him by the common law or by the statue.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Devki & others- Neutral Citation No. 2016:DHC:1735
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case of motor accident, it is imperative that the claimants show by some evidence that the driver of the motor vehicle had been negligent in relation to the said vehicle and thereby had caused an accident resulting in bodily injuries or death or damage to the property so as to be held liable as Pramila Rani & Others vs Phooleshwar & Another on 9 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon

entities.text: Pramila Rani & Others vs Phooleshwar & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65240140/
5 the principal tort-feasor.
The owner's liability arises out of his failure to discharge a duty cast on him by the law, on principal vicarious liability.
Proof of negligence is necessary before the owner or the insurance company may be held liable for payment of compensation in a motor accident claim case brought under Section 166 MV Act.

Should a claimant find it difficult to prove evidence with regard to negligence, the option to have resort to no fault liability on the structured formula under section 163-A of MV Act is always available to seek just compensation.
20. Section 166 of the MV Act is based on the principle of fault and negligence which has not been proved in this case.

Undisputedly, the petitioners/claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities, but in this case the evidence lead is either deficient or doubtful about the involvement of the offending vehicle and more particularly the act of rash and negligent act on its part.
Therefore, the petition under Section 166 of MV Act cannot be allowed.

This could have been a case if pleaded and proved accordingly under Section 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act but remedy for payment of compensation both under section 163A and section 166 being final and independent of each other as statutorily provided, a claimant cannot pursue his remedies thereunder simultaneously.
The claimant must opt/elect to go either for proceeding under section 163A or under section 166 of the Act, but not under both (Oriental insurance Co. Ltd vs Dhanbai Kanji Gandhi, AIR 2011 SC 1138).

entities.text: Oriental insurance Co. Ltd vs Dhanbai Kanji Gandhi, AIR 2011 SC 1138
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 21. Accordingly, this claim petition stands dismissed.
